questions.question: A thief moving at 40 km/h covers a distance in 5 hours 15 minutes. If the police chasing him cover the same distance at 50 km/h, then how long will the police take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Thief's speed = 40 km/h

Time taken by the thief = 5 hours 15 minutes = 5.25 hours

Police's speed = 50 km/h

**Concept:** Distance = Speed × Time.

**Solution:**

Distance covered by the thief = Speed × Time = 40 × 5.25 = 210 km.

Time taken by the police to cover the same distance = Distance/Speed = 210/50 = 4 hours 12 minutes

**Hence, the police will take 4 hours 12 minutes to cover the same distance.**

questions.question: A car can cover 275 km in 5 hours. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, then how much time will the car take to cover a distance of 300 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the car in 5 hours = 275 km

Distance to cover = 300 km

Speed reduction = 5 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Initial speed of the car = 275 km / 5 hr = 55 km/h

New speed = 55 km/h - 5 km/h = 50 km/h

Time to cover 300 km at 50 km/h

Time = 300 km / 50 km/h

Time = 6 hours

**The car will take 6 hours to cover a distance of 300 km at the reduced speed.**

questions.question: A boat travels a distance of 54 km at uniform speed. If the speed of boat is increased by 3 km/hr, then it takes 3 hours less to cover the same distance. What is the original speed of the boat?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A boat travels a distance of 54 km at uniform speed. If the speed of the boat is increased by 3 km/hr, then it takes 3 hours less to cover the same distance.

**Formula used:**

Let the original speed of the boat be x km/hr.

Time taken at original speed = Distance / Speed = 54 / x hours

Time taken at increased speed = Distance / (Speed + 3) = 54 / (x + 3) hours

According to the problem:

54 / x - 54 / (x + 3) = 3

**Calculations:**

54 / x - 54 / (x + 3) = 3

⇒ (54(x + 3) - 54x) / (x(x + 3)) = 3

⇒ (54x + 162 - 54x) / (x(x + 3)) = 3

⇒ 162 / (x² + 3x) = 3

⇒ 162 = 3(x² + 3x)

⇒ 162 = 3x² + 9x

⇒ 3x² + 9x - 162 = 0

⇒ x² + 3x - 54 = 0

⇒ (x + 9)(x - 6) = 0

⇒ x = -9 or x = 6

Since speed cannot be negative, x = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

questions.question: A person covered a certain distance at some speed. Had he moved 6 km/h faster, he would have taken 30 minutes less. If he had moved 4 km/h slower, he would have taken 30 minutes more. What is his original speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If the man moved 6 km/h faster, he would have taken 30 minutes less. If he had moved 4 km/h slower, he would have taken 30 minutes more.

**Concept Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the original speed be m km/h and the distance is x km

For the first case get,

x/m - x/(m + 6) = 30/60 [30 mins = 30/60 hours]

⇒ x(m + 6 - m)/m(m + 6) = 1/2

⇒ 6x/m(m + 6) = 1/2

⇒ x = m(m + 6)/12 ----(1)

Again from the 2nd case get,

x/(m - 4) - x/m = 30/60 [30 mins = 30/60 hours]

⇒ x(m - m + 4)/m(m - 4) = 1/2

⇒ x = m(m - 4)/8 ----(2)

From (1) and (2) get,

m(m + 6)/12 = m(m - 4)/8

⇒ 2(m² + 6m) = 3(m² - 4m)

⇒ 2m² + 12m = 3m² - 12m

⇒ m² - 24m = 0

⇒ m(m - 24) = 0

⇒ m = 0 or m = 24

m can't be 0 so, m = 24

**∴ original speed is 24kmph.**

questions.question: Excluding the stoppages, the speed of a truck is 90 km/h and including the stoppages, the speed of the truck is 36 km/h in a journey. For how many minutes does the truck stop per hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Stoppage time per hour = [(Speed without stoppage − Speed with stoppage) ÷ Speed without stoppage] × 60

⇒ Time = [(90 − 36) ÷ 90] × 60

⇒ Time = (54 ÷ 90) × 60

⇒ Time = 36 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the truck without stoppages = 90 km/h

Speed of the truck with stoppages = 36 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a930341d3e314e9d5694a0880ce163c5f393fbd22693ce58d82a676ac5211d4d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour without stoppage = 90 km

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour with stoppage = 36 km

⇒ Distance not covered due to stoppage = 90 − 36 = 54 km

⇒ The stoppage time is equal to the time required to cover this 54 km at the original speed without stoppage.

⇒ Time stopped = (54 ÷ 90) hours

⇒ Time stopped = (54 ÷ 90) × 60 minutes

⇒ Time stopped = 3 × 12 = 36 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Stoppage Time Formula

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed × 60 minutes.

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. If a journey is divided into two equal parts traveled at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2 × a × b) ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction at speeds a and b (a > b), their relative speed is (a − b). When moving in opposite directions, it is (a + b).
</p

⇒ x - S = 6 ---(1)

We know,

Sx = 187 km

questions.question: Amisha walks 3 km at a speed of 2 km/h, runs 7 km at a speed of 4 km/h and goes.another 32 km by bus. If the speed of the bus is 28 km/h, then find Amisha’s average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
**Data:**

Distance walked (d1) = 3 km, Speed (s1) = 2 km/h

Distance ran (d2) = 7 km, Speed (s2) = 4 km/h

Distance by bus (d3) = 32 km, Speed (s3) = 28 km/h

**Concept:**

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken.

**Solution:**

Calculate the time taken to walk 3 km.

⇒ Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ Time = 3 km / 2 km/h = 1.5 hours

Calculate the time taken to run 7 km.

⇒ Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ Time = 7 km / 4 km/h = 1.75 hours

Calculate the time taken to travel 32 km by bus.

⇒ Time = Distance/Speed

⇒ Time = 32 km / 28 km/h = 1.14 hours

Calculate the total distance travelled.

⇒ Total Distance = Distance walked + Distance run + Distance by bus

⇒ Total Distance = 3 km + 7 km + 32 km = 42 km

Calculate the total time taken.

⇒ Total Time = Time walking + Time running + Time by bus

⇒ Total Time = 1.5 hours + 1.75 hours + 1.14 hours = 4.39 hours

Calculate the average speed.

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 42 km / 4.39 hours = (392)/(41)km/h

**Hence, Amisha's average speed for the whole journey is (392)/(41)km/h km/h.**

questions.question: A person covered a distance of 250 km at a certain speed. If his speed is 20% less, he would have covered the same distance in 1(1)/(4) hours more time. His speed (in km/hr), initially was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed ratio** (Original : New) = 100% : 80% = 5 : 4

Since **distance** is constant, **Time ratio** is the inverse of speed ratio = 4 : 5

Difference in time ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 unit → 1¼ hours (5/4 hours)

Original time (4 units) = 4 × (5/4) = 5 hours

Original Speed = Total Distance ÷ Original Time = 250 ÷ 5 = 50 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (D) = 250 km

Speed reduction = 20%

Time increase (Δt) = 1¼ hours = 5/4 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60fc42c498b6a0bf14eb594c8298d15c12a2f59c535378b24583abe56440b1a8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original speed be S km/hr.

⇒ New speed = S − 20% of S = 0.8S km/hr.

⇒ Time taken initially (t₁) = 250/S

⇒ Time taken later (t₂) = 250/0.8S

⇒ t₂ − t₁ = 5/4

⇒ 250/0.8S − 250/S = 5/4

⇒ (250 × 1.25)/S − 250/S = 5/4

⇒ 312.5/S − 250/S = 5/4

⇒ 62.5/S = 5/4

⇒ S = (62.5 × 4) ÷ 5

⇒ S = 250 ÷ 5 = 50 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Inverse Proportionality

When **distance** is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Average Speed Formula

For the same distance covered at two different speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, relative speed is (S₁ − S₂); in the opposite direction, it is (S₁ + S₂).</p

questions.question: A teacher travelled a distance of 22 km in 7 hours. He travelled partly on foot at the speed of 2 km/h and partly on bicycle at the rate of 4 km/h. The distance travelled on foot is:
questions.solution:

A teacher travelled a distance of 22 km in 7 hours. He travelled partly on foot at the speed of 2 km/h and partly on bicycle at the rate of 4 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Let the distance travelled on foot be x km.

Time taken on foot = x / 2 hours

Distance travelled on bicycle = (22 - x) km

Time taken on bicycle = (22 - x) / 4 hours

Total time = 7 hours

**Calculation:**

x / 2 + (22 - x) / 4 = 7

⇒ 2x + 22 - x = 28

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The distance travelled on foot is 6 km. The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Ram covers 500 km distance in 20 hours in traffic; he covered some distance by bike at 30 km/h, and rest by car at 20 km/h. The distance covered by bike (in km) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed for the entire journey = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 500 ÷ 20 = 25 km/h.

Using alligation on speeds (Bike: 30 km/h, Car: 20 km/h, Average: 25 km/h):

Ratio of time taken = (25 − 20) : (30 − 25) = 5 : 5 = 1 : 1.

Time spent on the bike = 1/2 of 20 hours = 10 hours.

Distance covered by bike = Speed × Time = 30 × 10 = 300 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total distance = 500 km

Total time = 20 hours

Speed of bike = 30 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd1114e5717ad7e8eae7c3538a815d797ccec15a6b0588161cd26ede8fe8cc1d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the time traveled by bike be t hours.

⇒ Then, time traveled by car = (20 − t) hours.

⇒ Total Distance = Distance by bike + Distance by car

⇒ 30t + 20(20 − t) = 500

⇒ 30t + 400 − 20t = 500

⇒ 10t = 100

⇒ t = 10 hours

⇒ Distance covered by bike = Speed × Time = 30 × 10 = 300 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 300 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

It is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Overall Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Alligation in Speed and Distance

When applying the alligation cross-method on speeds, the resulting ratio strictly represents the ratio of the **time** taken at those speeds, not the ratio of distances covered.

Relative Speed

For bodies moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (v₁ + v₂). For bodies moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (|v₁ − v₂|).
</p

questions.question: A person travelled a distance of 60 km and then returned to the starting point. questions.question: From places A to B, which are 50 km apart, T covers half of the distance in 20 minutes. What should be his speed (in km/h) in the second half so that his average speed from A to B is 80 km/h?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

First half **speed** (v₁) = 25 km ÷ (20/60) h = 75 km/h.

When **distances** are equal, **Average Speed** = 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

80 = (2 × 75 × v₂) ÷ (75 + v₂)

80(75 + v₂) = 150v₂ ⇒ 6000 + 80v₂ = 150v₂.

70v₂ = 6000 ⇒ v₂ = 600 ÷ 7 ≈ 85.7 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 85.7 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total **Distance** = 50 km, **Average Speed** = 80 km/h, **First Half Time** = 20 min.

**Formula Used:** **Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3295248855f7a178d093d8c0cef42013b5db8de36499c799b9331575c7198613.png] 

⇒ Total **Time** = 50 ÷ 80 = 5/8 hours

⇒ **Time** for first half = 20 ÷ 60 = 1/3 hours

⇒ **Time** for second half = (5/8) − (1/3)

⇒ **Time** for second half = (15 − 8) ÷ 24 = 7/24 hours

⇒ **Speed** for second half = 25 ÷ (7/24)

⇒ **Speed** for second half = (25 × 24) ÷ 7 = 600 ÷ 7 ≈ 85.7 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 85.7 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

It is calculated as Total **Distance** ÷ Total **Time** taken for the entire journey.

Equal Distance Case

If a journey is divided into two equal **distances** with **speeds** v₁ and v₂, the average **speed** is the harmonic mean: 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **speed** from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.</p

⇒ 3000 = x² - 10x

⇒ x2 - 10x - 3000 = 0

⇒ x2 - 60x + 50x - 3000 = 0

⇒ x(x - 60) + 50(x - 60) = 0

⇒ (x - 60)(x + 50) = 0

⇒ x = 60 or -50

Since speed cannot be negative, so

∴ Usual speed of car, x = 60 km/hr
